To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a recently identified diabetes susceptibility gene is linked to β-cell dysfunction in lean Japanese individuals with type 2 (nonautoimmune) diabetes.
the type 2 diabetes–risk gene CDKAL1 associates with reduced GSIS in lean patients with type 1 diabetes and in lean patients with MODY3.
a recently identified risk gene for type 2 (T2DM), SLC30A8, associates with reduced GSIS in lean individuals with T2DM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genetic variants that influence the risk of type 2 diabetes, with a particular emphasis on the genes that are involved in the regulation of glucose metabolism in the pancreas.
understanding the genetic basis of β-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes and its relationship to the pathophysiology of the disease.
the identification and characterization of genes that contribute to type 2 diabetes susceptibility and progression in Japanese subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk gene identified in this report (8) is associated with a subset of lean individuals with type 2A diabetes.
the authors demonstrate that the rs7903146 T allele of the TCF7L 2 gene is associated with a reduced first-phase insulin response in a cohort of 100 lean Japanese individuals with type 2 disease.
the authors of this article (8) have provided a strong argument for the role of a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the HHEX gene in the development of diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the gene for the disease and found a mechanism that explains how the gene causes the disease.
a gene that is not expressed in the pancreas (or any other organ) associates with a β-cell dysfunction phenotype.
the risk for type 2 diabetic patients is a function of the risk for type-2 diabetic patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lean Japanese patients with diabetes are likely to have a defect in β-cell function.
a single SNP in the SLC30A8 gene associates with reduced GSIS in lean Japanese patients diagnosed with type 2 (or type 2-like) diabetes.
a common type 2 diabetes susceptibility allele is associated with impaired GSIS, even in the absence of obesity.
